title: Source-degenerated CS amp
description: A common-source stage with a source-degeneration resistor R_s. The degeneration lowers the effective transconductance to Gm = gm/(1 + gm*R_s) and raises the device output resistance by the same factor, so into an ideal load the intrinsic gain is unchanged; the payoff is linearity, since the stage transconductance is set by the (linear) resistor rather than the (nonlinear) device gm. The cost is R_s's own 4kT*R_s thermal noise, added directly at the input. The device source sits I_bias*R_s above ground, so the bind declares vsb = I_bias*R_s (body grounded); on a table without a vsb axis this is advisory and the body effect gmb is omitted. Sweep R_s to trade gain and noise against linearity.

params.name: V_out
params.note: drain DC level; the device vds is this minus the degenerated source level

params.name: R_load
params.note: load resistance presented to the stage output

params.name: R_s
params.note: degeneration resistor: larger R_s linearizes the stage (Gm -> 1/R_s) but lowers gain and adds 4kT*R_s noise

rows.name: Gm
rows.note: degenerated transconductance; approaches 1/R_s (resistor-set, linear) for gm*R_s >> 1

rows.name: loop
rows.note: degeneration factor: how far gm is traded for linearity and raised output resistance

rows.name: Rout_dev
rows.note: degeneration boosts the device output resistance by the same factor Gm is lowered

rows.name: Av
rows.note: degenerated transconductance into the load; into an ideal load Av -> gm/gds (gain preserved, linearity gained)

rows.name: vn_in
rows.note: channel noise is unchanged input-referred; the degeneration resistor adds 4kT*R_s directly at the input

rules.note: gm/ID cannot exceed the weak-inversion ceiling of the data
device saturated: the drain-to-source voltage is the drain level minus the I*R_s source lift
